q: Can you clean second-story windows without a ladder?
a: Often, yes. For high or hard to reach glass we use pure deionized water on a water-fed pole, which dries without leaving a spot. Where a ladder is the right tool we use one, safely.

q: What is a water-fed pole and is it better than squeegeeing?
a: A water-fed pole feeds pure deionized water up to a brush head, so we can reach high glass from the ground and it dries spot free. It has real advantages for height and for big commercial jobs. For most residential glass we hand wash, because being right at the glass is how we catch every detail and buff off mineral buildup. We use whichever gets your windows perfect.

q: How do professionals get windows streak-free?
a: Skill, the right technique, and working fast. In Arizona heat, solution dries on the glass before most people can pull it, which is where streaks come from. Our technicians are trained to work quickly and precisely, and we double check every pane before we leave.

q: Why do my windows look worse after I clean them myself?
a: Usually two things. First, the solution dried in the heat before it could be squeegeed. Second, the frames, sills, tracks, and screens were left dirty, so the next gust of wind put all that dust right back on the glass. That's exactly why we clean every part of the window.

q: Can hard water stains be removed from windows?
a: Mineral buildup sitting on the glass, yes. We buff it off with 0000 grade steel wool and it's included in every clean. What no one can fix is etching, where minerals have been left long enough to eat into the glass permanently. We'll tell you which one you have before you've paid for anything.

q: Is hard water spotting on glass permanent?
a: It can become permanent. Mineral deposits left on a window long enough etch into the glass, and etched glass has to be replaced rather than cleaned. Caught early, it comes right off. That's the single best reason to clean on a schedule.

q: What causes white spots on my windows in Arizona?
a: Hard water. Tucson's water is mineral heavy, and when water dries on glass it leaves the minerals behind. Rain, irrigation, and especially rinsing windows with a hose all cause it.

q: Can sprinkler overspray damage window glass?
a: Yes. Any mineral heavy water that dries on glass repeatedly will leave deposits, and deposits left long enough etch. If irrigation or hose water is regularly hitting your windows, that's worth addressing.

q: How do I stop sprinklers from spotting my windows?
a: Adjust any irrigation that's reaching the glass, and don't rinse windows with a hose thinking it helps. It makes things worse. If you've already got buildup, have it removed before it etches.

q: Can you clean windows with a broken or fogged seal?
a: We'll clean both surfaces, but the fog is inside the sealed unit and nobody can clean that. It's a failed seal, which means the glass unit needs replacing. We'll tell you before we start, not after.

q: Why is there condensation between my double-pane windows?
a: The seal has failed and moisture has gotten into the space between the panes. It's a glass problem, not a cleaning problem, and the unit needs to be replaced.

q: Can window cleaners fix a foggy double-pane window?

q: Do solar panels need to be cleaned in Arizona?
a: More than almost anywhere. Desert dust, pollen, and mineral residue build up constantly, and there's rarely enough rain to clear it. A layer of dust blocks light before it ever reaches the cell.

q: How much production do dirty solar panels lose?
a: Research puts it anywhere from 5 to 30 percent depending on how much has built up and local conditions. Your actual number depends on your panels. That's why we take before and after photos on every job, so you can see the difference yourself.

q: How often should solar panels be cleaned in Tucson?
a: Once or twice a year keeps them performing and protects the glass from mineral damage.

q: Does rain clean solar panels well enough?
a: No, and this is the most common misconception we hear. Rain moves dust around rather than removing it, and the dust sticks. Then the water dries and leaves mineral spots. Panels need actual scrubbing with a brush and soap to come clean.

q: Why do my solar panels have white spots after it rains?
a: Minerals. Tucson's water is hard, and when rain dries on the panel glass it leaves deposits behind. That's part of why rain doesn't clean panels, it can actually add to the problem.

q: Can I clean my own solar panels?
a: You can, but there's real risk. Getting on a roof, cracking a panel, using the wrong water, or spraying it with a hose that leaves mineral spots. If you do it yourself, no pressure washer, no stiff brushes, and don't walk on the panels. Or give us a call and we'll handle it safely.

q: Will cleaning solar panels void my warranty?
a: Not the way we do it. We avoid harsh chemicals and stiff brushes specifically to protect your panels and your warranty. If you have questions about your specific manufacturer's terms, we're happy to talk it through.

q: Is it safe to walk on solar panels to clean them?
a: No. Standing on panels is how microcracks happen. We work from the roof surface and with the right equipment.

q: What water should be used to clean solar panels?
a: Deionized water is ideal because it dries clean and leaves nothing behind. We use it along with hand washing and soap when the buildup calls for it.

q: What is deionized water and why is it used on solar panels?
a: It's water with the dissolved minerals removed. Regular water leaves mineral deposits when it dries, which is exactly what you're trying to get rid of. Deionized water dries spot free.

q: Can pressure washing damage solar panels?
a: Yes. High pressure can crack panels and force water into places it shouldn't be. We never pressure wash solar panels.

q: Should soap or detergent be used on solar panels?

q: How do you remove bird droppings from solar panels?

q: Do birds nesting under solar panels cause damage?

q: Does dust really reduce solar panel output in the desert?
a: Yes. Dust on the glass blocks light before it reaches the cell. Southern Arizona has more airborne dust than almost anywhere, and panels can go months without meaningful rain.

q: How often should windows be cleaned in Tucson?
a: Three times a year. That's what it takes in this climate to keep windows clean and to stop mineral buildup before it etches the glass. The natural timing is right after summer and monsoon season, around the holidays, and in spring.

q: How often should you clean windows in a desert climate?
a: More often than most places. Desert dust is year round and the water is hard, so buildup never really stops. Three times a year is the right rhythm for Tucson.

q: Is twice a year enough for window cleaning in Arizona?
a: Three times a year is what we recommend for Tucson. Twice a year leaves a long gap where dust and minerals build up, and that's when etching starts.

q: When is the best time of year to clean windows in Tucson?
a: Three natural points. Right after summer and monsoon season, when everything is covered in dust. Around the holidays, so your home is ready for guests and the new year. And in spring, when pollen adds to the usual buildup.

q: Should I clean windows before or after monsoon season?
a: After. Monsoon storms leave heavy dirt and dust behind. Cleaning right after summer resets everything going into fall.

q: Do windows get dirtier faster near open desert?
a: Yes, noticeably. Open exposure means more airborne dust reaching the glass.

q: How often should I clean windows if I have sprinklers?
a: If irrigation water is regularly hitting your glass, it's worth adjusting it and keeping a regular cleaning schedule, since that mineral spotting etches over time. Three times a year handles it for most homes.

q: Does dust from dirt roads make windows dirtier?
a: Considerably. Unpaved roads, horse properties, and open desert all put more dust in the air.

q: How often should snowbirds schedule window cleaning?
a: Most seasonal residents have us come right when they arrive, so the house is clean and ready the day they get to Tucson. Tell us your arrival date and we'll have it scheduled.

q: Should I clean windows before selling my house?
a: Yes. Clean windows make a home look well kept, in person and in listing photos. Real estate agents use us for exactly this, and every agent who's hired us once has kept coming back.

q: Does clean glass actually help a home sell faster?
a: We won't claim a number, but clean windows make a home present better, and that's what listing photos and showings turn on. Every real estate agent who's tried us has continued using us.

q: Can neglected windows be permanently damaged?
a: Yes. Minerals left on glass long enough etch into it permanently, and etched glass gets replaced, not cleaned. Regular cleaning prevents that entirely.

q: What happens if you never clean your windows?
a: Dust and minerals build up, the buildup etches the glass, and eventually it's a replacement cost instead of a cleaning bill. Replacing windows costs dramatically more than maintaining them.

q: How do I keep my windows clean longer between visits?
a: Don't rinse them with a hose. It feels like it helps but it leaves mineral deposits that lead to etching. Keep irrigation off the glass. And clean on a schedule so buildup never gets ahead of you. Our 5-in-1 Deep Clean also keeps windows cleaner longer, because there's no dust left in the tracks and screens to blow back onto the glass.

q: Is professional window cleaning worth the money?
a: It protects the glass, not just the view. Hard water left on a pane long enough etches it permanently, and etched glass has to be replaced. Maintaining your windows is far cheaper than replacing them, and with us you don't pay until you're happy.

q: Won't my windows just get dirty again?
a: Everything does eventually. But most cleaning leaves dust in the tracks, frames, and screens, so the next gust blows it right back onto the glass. Our 5-in-1 Deep Clean removes all of it, so windows stay clean much longer. Between that, three visits a year, and the 14-Day Spotless Guarantee, your windows stay clean essentially year round.

q: Can I just clean my own windows?
a: You can, and if you enjoy it, go for it. It's harder than it looks, though. Getting glass truly streak free in Arizona heat takes skill and speed. Scrapers scratch glass if used wrong. Ladders and step stools are where people get hurt. And if you don't clean the tracks and screens too, the dust comes right back. Whatever you do, don't just hose them off. That accelerates the damage.

q: What do professional window cleaners do that I can't?
a: Get every pane streak free in the heat, buff off mineral buildup safely, clean every part of the window so the results last, handle height safely, and do the whole house in a few hours. And guarantee it.

q: Is Dawn dish soap good for cleaning windows?
a: It cuts grease but leaves a film that attracts dust and streaks in sun. It's not what we use.

q: Does vinegar and newspaper actually clean windows?
a: It sort of works on small panes, but it's slow, streaky, and useless on hard water buildup.

q: Why do my windows streak when I clean them?
a: Usually the solution dried in the heat before you could pull it, or the squeegee edge wasn't clean. Arizona sun makes it especially tough.

q: Is a pressure washer safe to use on windows?
a: No. Pressure can force water past seals and damage frames. Windows are hand work.

q: Are window cleaning robots any good?
a: They're fine for maintenance on flat interior glass. They don't handle frames, sills, tracks, screens, mineral buildup, or exteriors.

q: Should I hire a handyman or a window cleaning company?
a: A handyman with a squeegee will clean the glass. A window cleaning company cleans the whole window, handles mineral buildup, has the right equipment for height, is insured specifically for the work, and guarantees the result.

q: What is the difference between window cleaning and window washing?
a: Nothing. Same service, different words. Our customers use both about equally, and so do we.

q: How do I compare window cleaning quotes fairly?
a: Check three things. Is it per pane or something vaguer, does it include screens and tracks or just glass, and what's the guarantee. A cheaper number that's glass only isn't actually cheaper.

q: What guarantee should a window cleaner offer?
a: At minimum, that you don't pay until you're happy. Ours goes further with a walkthrough before payment and a 14-Day Spotless Guarantee on top.

q: What does a satisfaction guarantee actually cover?

q: Do you offer solar panel pigeon proofing?
a: Yes. We install exclusion mesh around the perimeter of your array so birds can't nest underneath, and we clean out any existing nesting and droppings first.

q: How does pigeon proofing attach to solar panels?
a: It clips on. No drilling into your roof and nothing attached to the panel frames. A one-way locking clip system holds the mesh in place. Nothing is penetrated and nothing is damaged.

q: Will pigeon proofing void my solar warranty?
a: No. Because we don't drill or attach anything to the panels, your solar warranty and your roof are completely untouched.

q: What do you do with the birds?
a: We encourage them to leave and fly off, then clean out everything they left behind. We're careful with wildlife and careful with you, since droppings are a genuine biohazard. We wear protective gear, bag everything, and haul it away so you never touch it.

q: Is pigeon proofing cheaper than calling pest control?
a: Customers have told us we came in at a fraction of what pest control quoted them for the same work. Pest control is where most people look first, but we're already on the roof, we clean the panels while we're there, and we include a warranty.

q: Should I get pigeon proofing if I don't have birds yet?
a: It's actually the cheapest time to do it. Installing exclusion before birds find your panels means no cleanup, which is most of the cost. It will never be cheaper than it is right now.

q: Do you install solar screens?
a: Yes. We custom measure, build, and install new solar screens, and we repair and rescreen existing ones.

q: What is the difference between solar screens and sun screens?
a: Same thing. Some people say sun screens, some say solar screens, some even say blackout screens. We use top-grade Phifer materials in any color and any shade percentage, most commonly 80 or 90 percent.

q: How much heat do solar screens block?
a: Up to 80 to 90 percent of the sun's heat and glare, depending on the mesh. They also block roughly 75 to 90 percent of UV, which protects furniture and flooring from fading.

q: Will solar screens make my house dark?
a: Barely. The view gets slightly darker and a touch less crisp, and most people are surprised how well they can still see out, even through 90 percent mesh.

q: Can people see in through solar screens?
a: No. From the outside looking in, you can't see through them at all. Daytime privacy without giving up your view is one of the real benefits.

q: Which windows should I put solar screens on?
a: West-facing windows first, since afternoon sun hits them hardest. Then south-facing. Really, any window that gets sun is worth it, and plenty of people do the whole house for full protection and a consistent look.

q: Do solar screens save on cooling costs?
a: Yes. The U.S. Department of Energy reports that well-placed shade can cut annual cooling costs by 7 to 15 percent, and Arizona installers commonly report even more. Solar screens are a genuine long-term investment in this climate.

q: How long do solar screens last?
a: Typically around a decade, and at least five years. Fading is what eventually wears them out, which is why we use top-grade materials.

q: How long does it take to get solar screens installed?
a: Usually two to three weeks from measure to install.

q: Do solar screens come with a warranty?

q: Can I remove solar screens myself?

q: Do you clean solar screens?

q: Do you repair screens or replace them?
a: Both. Repair means replacing the mesh and keeping your frame. If the frame itself is too far gone, we'll tell you replacement makes more sense, even though repair is the smaller job.

q: How long does screen repair take?
